label: copy phase, L=9, step outputting the 4th original token (rare, token-combination gated)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, with weak activations (max 0.011), almost always in L=9 sequences (89% of mass). It sits at the step that outputs original token 3 (t=12, input = orig(2)): 84% of mass. A smaller cluster is at the final step (recall_idx 8, 8% of mass), and a few cases are in L=8 at recall_idx 3. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on the first occurrence of a token. Its position is well defined, but it fires on only ~1.6% of the steps at that position. Which steps depends on token identity: input orig(2) in {w,k,v,f,z,a} with orig(1) being h or a digit gives about 6x higher rates. Adding these token sets only reaches ~7-10% precision while losing recall. So the position explains most of the mass, but the token combination that gates firing was not captured. Not checked: what modulates magnitude beyond the top examples, which are these same w/k/v/f/z tokens after h or a digit.
